subject: Geopolitics
title: Space as Sovereign Territory
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Space as Sovereign Territory.

hook.text: The 1967 Outer Space Treaty says no nation can own the Moon. But no one enforced that when Artemis launched.

buildup.text: As space becomes commercially valuable — mining, satellites, bases — nations push to claim extraterrestrial zones.

discovery.text: Orbital slots and lunar landing sites are already contested. First-mover advantage applies beyond Earth.

twist.text: The Artemis Accords let signatories create safety zones around lunar sites. Critics call them soft land grabs.

climax.text: Space borders may soon matter. Water ice on the Moon and minerals on asteroids are worth trillions.

punchline.text: The border dispute of the future is above our heads.

quiz.question: What does the 1967 Outer Space Treaty prohibit?
